lead.headline: Mastercard's $1.8B BVNK acquisition closes as BlackRock and Kenya push tokenized assets mainstream, while Coldcard hardware wallets suffer $116M exploit
lead.tldr: Institutional stablecoin infrastructure is accelerating through M&A and tokenized fund launches, even as self-custody security assumptions face their most serious stress test since the industry's early days.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today the tension between institutional adoption velocity and foundational security assumptions defines where capital will and will not flow in the coming quarter.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin owners rocked by $116 million hack: What we know about the Coldcard exploit
top_signals.summary: A massive security breach has targeted Coldcard cold storage wallets, resulting in the theft of 1,816 Bitcoin. The exploit is particularly concerning as it compromised wallets previously considered hyper-secure.

top_signals.title: Mastercard completes $1.8B BVNK acquisition in stablecoin push15m, Mastercard completes $1.8B BVNK acquisition in stablecoin pushMastercard said the tie-up would help banks, fintechs and enterprises expand stablecoin payments, payouts, settlement and treasury services.
top_signals.summary: Mastercard has finalized the acquisition of BVNK for $1.8 billion to strengthen its stablecoin capabilities. The move aims to provide banks and fintechs with enhanced tools for stablecoin payments, settlements, and treasury services.

top_signals.title: BlackRock launches two tokenized money market funds for stablecoin reserves
top_signals.summary: BlackRock has launched two tokenized money market funds specifically designed to hold stablecoin reserves. This move places the asset manager alongside other financial giants like Morgan Stanley and Fidelity in providing institutional-grade reserve solutions.

top_signals.title: BlackRock launches tokenized money market funds for stablecoin reserves37m
top_signals.summary: BlackRock has introduced tokenized money market funds specifically designed to serve as reserves for stablecoins. This move integrates traditional financial liquidity management with blockchain-based digital assets.

top_signals.title: Kenya moves 30 million academic credentials onto Avalanche blockchain4m, Kenya moves 30 million academic credentials onto Avalanche blockchainA new digital verification platform aims to reduce forged certificates by allowing employers and universities to authenticate academic records onchain.
top_signals.summary: Kenya is migrating 30 million academic credentials to the Avalanche blockchain to create a digital verification platform. The initiative aims to eliminate the use of forged certificates by enabling employers and universities to authenticate records on-chain.

on_the_radar.title: HashKey receives JPMorgan approval to open client money account58m
on_the_radar.summary: HashKey has received approval from JPMorgan to open a client money account, marking a significant bridge between traditional finance and digital asset services. This move enhances the legitimacy and operational capacity of the crypto exchange within the regulated banking system.

on_the_radar.title: ZeroStack Warns of Survival Risk After $82.5M Crypto Loss
on_the_radar.summary: ZeroStack has warned that its continued operation is in doubt following a massive crypto loss of $82.5 million. The company currently holds only $2.6 million in cash, posing a severe survival risk.

on_the_radar.title: Kalshi and Polymarket's combined volume reaches all-time high in July, surpassing $50 billion
on_the_radar.summary: Prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket saw a combined trading volume surge to an all-time high of over $50 billion in July. While the main Polymarket platform experienced a volume dip, Polymarket US saw a significant increase of 54%.

on_the_radar.title: Boltz pauses service after wave of AI-assisted hacking attempts
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin swap service Boltz has suspended its operations following a series of AI-assisted hacking attempts. The service paused to prevent further losses as attackers were adapting exploits faster than the development team could deploy patches.

on_the_radar.title: DEXs capture record 24% of spot crypto trading as CEX volumes sink
on_the_radar.summary: Decentralized exchanges (DEXs) have reached a record 24% share of spot crypto trading volume. This growth comes as centralized exchange (CEX) spot volumes decline toward a 12-month low.

on_the_radar.title: Bithumb sets 2028 IPO timetable as it overhauls internal controls
on_the_radar.summary: South Korean exchange Bithumb has outlined a timeline to go public, aiming for a preliminary listing review in 2027 and a full IPO by 2028. The move comes alongside an overhaul of internal controls following a significant crediting error.

on_the_radar.title: Michael Saylor's Strategy sells another 1,638 BTC for $105 million, reducing total holdings to 842,138 BTC
on_the_radar.summary: MicroStrategy has sold 1,638 BTC worth approximately $105 million. This reduces their total holdings to 842,138 BTC, which still represents about 4% of the total Bitcoin supply.

on_the_radar.title: CLARITY Act failure could send crypto valuations lower: Bernstein
on_the_radar.summary: Bernstein warns that the failure of the CLARITY Act to pass could lead to a decline in cryptocurrency valuations. The firm suggests this outcome may accelerate the need for policy guidance from the SEC and CFTC.

linkedin_post:
Stablecoin infrastructure is being bought, not built. Mastercard paid $1.8 billion for BVNK. BlackRock launched tokenized money market funds specifically to sit behind stablecoin reserves. Kenya put 30 million academic credentials on Avalanche. Each of these assumes the rails work.

Then Coldcard. 1,816 Bitcoin taken from hardware wallets that were supposed to be air-gapped, offline, beyond remote reach. The exploit vector matters less than what it breaks: the core assumption that self-custody hardware is categorically safer than institutional custody for large holdings.

We are underwriting the stablecoin sector on payment volume growth and reserve yield compression. The Coldcard event reprices the custody layer beneath that. Institutional custody providers just saw their competitive moat widen against hardware solutions that cannot demonstrate tamper-proof supply chains or firmware integrity.

The test: whether any hardware wallet vendor can produce a third-party audit of their entire manufacturing and update pipeline within 90 days. Those that cannot will lose institutional and high-net-worth flows to custodied alternatives. Those that can may capture a premium.

Mastercard and BlackRock are not betting on self-custody. They are betting on regulated, auditable, intermediated rails. The gap between those two worlds just grew.
